subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Trolley Problem and Moral Intuition
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Trolley Problem and Moral Intuition.

hook.text: Divert a trolley to kill one instead of five? Most say yes. Push a man off a bridge? Most say no.

buildup.text: Both scenarios save five lives. But the physical act of pushing triggers a visceral gut response.

discovery.text: Greene's brain scans show impersonal dilemmas fire reason areas. Personal ones fire emotion areas.

twist.text: Patients with damage to emotion areas make cold utilitarian choices every time. Five beats one.

climax.text: Moral judgment is a negotiation between gut feeling and deliberation—and the gut often wins.

punchline.text: Morality isn't math. Feelings vote too.

quiz.question: What did Joshua Greene's brain scans reveal about moral judgment?
options: All moral decisions are purely logical
Brain scans show no moral activity
